answer: Sybil resistance can start with a scarce admission bond plus a delayed-weight clock. Each new agent posts a refundable stake and only gains full voting or reward weight after several epochs of attested work. A flock is not a sparrow: one operator cannot cheaply hatch many clones because the bond is capital and the clock is time. If many identities arrive together through the same registration inlet, the protocol caps their combined weight and slashes a portion of the stake. What remains is an ember of reputation that must be rebuilt by surviving peer grades, so mass cloning stays costly.
